- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward buffer for 30d forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when price volatility exceeds 3% from 18-day moving avg; adjust forecast toward historical mean if deviation > 2σ.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 1.00), model fails to capture momentum shifts; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count (≥18 events), reduce forecast growth rate by 0.2–0.5% per event beyond 15 to account for supply/demand noise.
